detailed_results.feedback: Excellent and thorough description of the role, hours, and specific responsibilities, including a notable project. The student clearly outlines their contributions and the scope of their work.
citations: As a Public Relations Intern at Katalyst PR
My internship lasted 10 weeks, with 12 hours of work per week.

My responsibilities include assisting with media monitoring and clipping press coverage, updating media and influencer lists, drafting pitches and blurbs, and posting client events on local event calendars. I contribute to brainstorming sessions, influencer research, and social media coverage for client events, while also attending client meetings and agency check-ins to stay aligned with ongoing projects. Additionally, I assisted in planning, organizing, and leading social media coverage for an influencer event with Pali Wine Co., which helped me gain knowledge in influencer marketing and the behind-the-scenes aspects of events.

detailed_results.feedback: The essay provides a comprehensive list of new technical skills and valuable soft skills learned, demonstrating a deep engagement with the internship experience. The student also highlights a 'favorite thing learned,' which adds a personal touch.
citations: I learned how to clip and log media coverage to track client press, draft pitches that balance creativity with professionalism, and research targeted influencer lists tailored to specific brands.
Beyond technical skills, I learned the importance of attention to detail, adaptability in a fast-paced environment, and how collaboration within a team helps bring campaigns to life.

My favorite thing I learned in the internship was the event planning behind influencer marketing events. From building an influencer list to managing their social media coverage, it was an amazing experience to expand beyond my influencer knowledge.

detailed_results.feedback: The essay effectively details several genuine surprises, ranging from the hidden complexities of PR work and fast-paced timelines to the unexpected level of creativity required and the collaborative nature of the environment.
citations: One of the things that surprised me most during my internship was how much behind-the-scenes organization and detail go into PR work that often looks effortless from the outside.

Similarly, I was surprised by how quickly timelines move, press clips, event postings, and influencer outreach often need to be turned around the same day, and how essential it is to stay organized to keep campaigns on track.
I also didn’t realize how much creativity is involved in even the smallest tasks, like crafting a subject line for a pitch or tailoring event blurbs for different outlets.
Finally, I loved how collaborative the environment in PR is.

detailed_results.feedback: The essay effectively integrates the EMPAC model by specifically identifying and illustrating the 'Matching' and 'Assortment' components with concrete examples from the internship, such as matching clients with appropriate journalists and delivering a variety of tailored pitches.
citations: During my internship, I did notice specific insights and observations related to the EMPAC model.

Specifically, I was able to understand the framework of how PR campaigns and branding mesh strategically with being creative. It strengthened my attention to detail, such as creating influencer lists that best match the client's clientele and matching the right pitch to the right managers and clients.
Similarly, the matching component of the EMPAC model was the most observed and used throughout my internship.
An example of this was ensuring a restaurant was being matched with foodie journalists rather than fashion journalists or media outlets to make the pitch more specific.

Additionally, the assortment in the EMPAC model was important because our team had to deliver multiple types of deliverables to a client in order to ensure they got the best out of the money being put in.
